## Recommended brand universe

For a North American hotel-plus-residential project, I would begin with the following brands—but shortlist them according to the project’s location, buyer profile, density and achievable residential pricing.

### 1. Proven, broad-market luxury leaders

| Brand | Best suited to | Principal advantage | Watch-outs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Four Seasons** | Trophy urban, coastal, mountain and golf resorts | Probably the deepest dedicated residential operating platform and strong recognition among global buyers | Highly selective; demanding design, amenity, staffing and capital standards |
| **The Ritz-Carlton** | Urban towers and destination resorts | Powerful consumer recognition, established residential program and Marriott Bonvoy ecosystem | Brand standards and shared hotel-residential facilities can be expensive |
| **St. Regis** | Formal luxury, gateway cities, ski and beach resorts | Strong luxury positioning and residential sales credibility | Best where the market supports traditional, high-touch luxury |
| **Waldorf Astoria** | Landmark urban and resort projects | Strong luxury name with a rapidly expanding Hilton residential platform | Residential track record is smaller than Four Seasons or Ritz-Carlton in some markets |
| **Mandarin Oriental** | High-end urban condominiums and select resorts | Strong international HNW recognition; works with both hotel-attached and standalone residences | Requires a truly prime site and sophisticated luxury demand |

Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton and St. Regis have historically occupied the leading hotel-brand positions in the Americas, while Marriott remains the largest parent company in the regional branded-residence sector. Four Seasons currently identifies 42 North American residential locations, demonstrating the scale of its regional platform. ([pdf.euro.savills.co.uk](https://pdf.euro.savills.co.uk/global-research/branded-residences-americas-23-24.pdf?utm_source=openai))

### 2. Ultra-luxury and scarcity brands

Consider these when the site can support very high pricing, low density and exceptional design:

- **Aman** — Best for ultra-private urban or destination projects with very limited inventory. Its North American portfolio includes New York, Amangiri, Amangani and developments in Beverly Hills, Miami Beach and Texas Hill Country. ([aman.com](https://www.aman.com/residences?utm_source=openai))
- **Rosewood** — Strong “sense of place” positioning for intimate city, coastal and resort developments; its current North American residential activity includes Beverly Hills, Naples and Los Cabos. ([rosewoodhotels.com](https://www.rosewoodhotels.com/en/residences?utm_source=openai))
- **One&Only** — Particularly compelling for large-format villas and destination resorts. It has demonstrated the model in Riviera Nayarit, Big Sky and the Hudson Valley. ([oneandonlyresorts.com](https://www.oneandonlyresorts.com/private-homes?utm_source=openai))
- **Raffles** — Appropriate for a landmark, internationally oriented ultra-luxury project, especially where distinctive F&B and service can be monetized.
- **Six Senses** — Best for wellness-led, environmentally sensitive resorts where the wellness proposition materially differentiates the residences.

These brands can create scarcity and pricing power, but generally require unusually strong real estate, architecture, amenities and developer credentials.

### 3. North American resort and residential specialists

| Brand | Best application |
|---|---|
| **Montage** | Ultra-luxury ski, golf, coastal and wine-country resorts |
| **Pendry** | Younger, design-conscious luxury buyers in urban, resort and entertainment-oriented markets |
| **Auberge Collection** | Site-specific boutique resorts and affluent second-home destinations |
| **1 Hotels / 1 Homes** | Sustainability-, wellness- and design-led urban or resort projects |

Montage explicitly treats residential as a core part of its development model, while Pendry provides a more contemporary and somewhat broader luxury positioning. Auberge has an extensive North American resort pipeline and emphasizes individually conceived hotels and residences rather than a standardized design formula. ([auberge.com](https://auberge.com/development/?utm_source=openai))

1 Hotels should be considered where sustainability is an authentic part of the development rather than simply a marketing overlay. Its existing residential projects include South Beach, Brooklyn and Cabo, with San Miguel de Allende in development. ([1hotels.com](https://www.1hotels.com/homes?utm_source=openai))

### 4. Lifestyle and younger-buyer brands

For markets such as Miami, Nashville, Austin, Los Angeles, Mexico City or selected mixed-use districts, evaluate:

- **EDITION**
- **W**
- **Pendry**
- **Thompson**
- **Andaz**
- **SLS**
- **NoMad**
- **1 Hotels**

These brands may produce stronger differentiation and social/F&B activation than traditional luxury flags. The trade-off is that some have shorter residential operating histories and may be more sensitive to changing design and lifestyle trends.

Hyatt’s residential platform now includes Park Hyatt, Thompson, Andaz, The Standard and Miraval, with more than 50 open or pipeline residential projects globally. Hilton is also broadening beyond Waldorf Astoria and Conrad into LXR, NoMad, Curio, Canopy and other brands. ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/may-30-2025-unscriptedbyhyatt?utm_source=openai))

### 5. Flexible collection brands

If the owner wants to retain a project-specific identity, consider:

- **The Luxury Collection**
- **Autograph Collection**
- **LXR Hotels & Resorts**
- **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt**
- **Curio Collection by Hilton**
- **Vignette Collection**
- Potentially **Tribute Portfolio** for a less expensive positioning

These can be useful when the site, architecture or existing hotel name already has equity. Autograph Collection is especially noteworthy: current market research forecasts significant growth in its branded-residential pipeline through 2032. ([brandedresi.com](https://brandedresi.com/savills-branded-residences-report-the-americas/?utm_source=openai))

### 6. Premium rather than ultra-luxury opportunities

Where achievable residential pricing cannot support an ultra-luxury service model, consider:

- **Westin**
- **Fairmont**
- **Kimpton**
- **Canopy by Hilton**
- **InterContinental**
- **Grand Hyatt**
- **Marriott or Sheraton residences**, selectively

Fairmont is particularly relevant in Canada, established resort markets and locations where heritage and destination recognition matter. Westin may work where wellness, global distribution and a somewhat more accessible residential price point are priorities.

## Suggested shortlist by project type

### Trophy urban tower
1. Four Seasons  
2. Ritz-Carlton  
3. St. Regis  
4. Mandarin Oriental  
5. Waldorf Astoria  
6. Aman or Rosewood, if the economics support ultra-luxury scarcity  

### Coastal, golf or mountain resort
1. Four Seasons  
2. Montage  
3. Auberge  
4. One&Only  
5. Rosewood  
6. Ritz-Carlton  
7. Aman, for an exceptional low-density site  

### Contemporary urban mixed-use project
1. EDITION  
2. Pendry  
3. W  
4. Thompson  
5. Andaz  
6. 1 Hotels  
7. NoMad or SLS  

### Wellness or nature-led resort
1. Six Senses  
2. Miraval  
3. 1 Hotels  
4. Aman  
5. Auberge  
6. One&Only  

### Distinctive independent hotel seeking distribution
1. Autograph Collection  
2. Luxury Collection  
3. LXR  
4. Unbound Collection  
5. Curio Collection  
6. Vignette Collection  

## How I would run the selection process

An owner should generally **screen eight to ten brands and issue a detailed RFP to four to six**, rather than choosing solely on brand prestige. Evaluate each proposal on:

1. **Residence pricing and absorption** supported by actual comparable transactions.
2. **Total fee burden**, including license, technical-services, sales-and-marketing, management and recurring residential fees.
3. **Incremental construction cost** created by brand standards.
4. **Required hotel size and economics**—some brands need a larger or more amenity-intensive hotel than the market supports.
5. **Residential staffing and HOA cost**, especially 24-hour service, housekeeping, concierge, security and F&B.
6. **Attached versus standalone model** and which facilities residents may use.
7. **Rental-program requirements** and restrictions on owner occupancy.
8. **Brand involvement in residential sales**, not merely permission to use the name.
9. **Area protection and competitive branded-residence supply**.
10. **Term, termination and debranding provisions**, including what happens to owners if the hotel management agreement ends.
11. **Cost-allocation and governance documents** governing the hotel, residences and shared amenities.
12. **Actual residential team and track record**, rather than the size of the hotel company generally.

## Bottom line

For most serious North American luxury projects, the initial benchmark set should be:

**Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, Waldorf Astoria, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Montage and Auberge.**

Then add:

- **Aman or One&Only** for exceptional ultra-luxury resorts;
- **EDITION, W, Pendry, Thompson or 1 Hotels** for lifestyle-oriented demand; and
- **Autograph Collection, Luxury Collection, LXR or Unbound** where flexibility and local identity are important.

The best brand is not necessarily the one claiming the largest residential premium. It is the brand whose attainable sales pricing and absorption exceed its incremental construction, fee, operating and HOA costs over the entire agreement term.
